text:
incident-bot: PAGED SEV2 - GPU hotpath queues rising across us-west, sustained 429 rate increase. alert: hotpath_queue_length > 10000 for 3m, gpu_pool_util=98% :rotating_light:
maria (oncall): ack — I'm on it. seeing a big queue spike and sustained 429s from downstream. which customers hit?
raj: seeing 429 surge concentrated on model v2-large endpoints and everything routed to hotpool-1. metrics: 429_rate ~= 18% for the last 5m, queue growth +12k/s.
ahmed: checking autoscaler logs — requests to allocate more GPUs are being rejected: "scale_request_denied: tier_quota_exceeded". looks like the tier policy cap prevented scale beyond 40 instances.
linda: wait we rolled a new tier policy config yesterday that caps hotpool tiers to 40 to control spend. that might be the cause.
maria (oncall): that's consistent. autoscaler tried to scale but hit tier cap. can we temporarily bump the tier cap?
raj: I can push a quick emergency override to the tier config. but want to also reduce load by routing to lower-cost backends to buy time.
ops-bot: runbook link: https://runbooks.internal/redwood/gpu-saturation — recommended actions: 1) emergency-tier-override, 2) apply tokenbucket throttle relax on critical customers, 3) route non-critical to fallback-model
ahmed: logs snippet from autoscaler (latest):
```
2026-03-15T14:07:22Z INFO scale_request for pool hotpath-1 -> requested=60
2026-03-15T14:07:22Z ERROR scale_request_denied: tier_quota_exceeded (tier:hotpath-prod, cap:40)
2026-03-15T14:07:22Z WARN queue_length=11234 inflight=6200
```
raj: I'm going to apply emergency override now: `infractl tiers update hotpath-prod --max-instances 120 --reason "emergency scale"`
raj: applied. CLI returned success. autoscaler attempting new scaling requests.
(2m later)
ahmed: autoscaler logs now show new scale in progress, but we're still seeing 429s because token bucket refill rates per-tier are aggressive for fairness and currently starving bursty customers. token count per-second is low.
linda: can we temporarily increase token refill for hotpath tier? e.g., from 100/s to 400/s?
maria (oncall): yes, do both. tier cap increased + token refill bump. also route non-critical embeddings to dedicated-embedding-pool. raj can you update routing policy?
raj: routing change in progress: `routeset apply --from hotpath-1 --to fallback-small-model --matcher "client_tags != enterprise"`
raj: routing applied. starting to see shift: traffic to fallback-small-model +22%
ahmed: tokenbucket change applied: `policyctl tokenbucket set hotpath-prod --refill 400 --burst 800` — command returned OK.
(3m later)
ops-bot: monitoring — gpu_pool_util dropped from 98% -> 82%, queue_length dropping: 11.2k -> 4.1k, 429_rate now 6%.
maria (oncall): good. continue to monitor while autoscaler finishes adding nodes. if 429s still >2% after nodes added, we'll need to adjust batching or KV cache settings.
ahmed: autoscaler finished scale, added 48 instances. pool size now ~88. queue draining steadily.
linda: customer impact — partial degraded responses for ~12 enterprise customers on us-west for ~18 minutes. ops notified support to triage customer tickets.
raj: note: the root cause is the recent tier policy rollout that set conservative max instances + low token refill to limit cost. that combination prevented autoscaler from responding to sudden sustained load.
maria (oncall): immediate mitigation summary: 1) emergency tier cap increased to 120; 2) tokenbucket refill increased to 400/s, burst 800; 3) routing traffic to fallback model for non-enterprise clients; 4) scaled up hotpath pool via autoscaler. 429s decreased from 18% -> 1.2% over 12 minutes. :white_check_mark:
ahmed: collecting metrics for postmortem: time window, affected model ids, customers, exact config diffs. will push to incident channel.
raj: we should also add an autoscaler pre-check in the tier rollout process to warn if new caps are below expected peak demand.
linda: agree. and add automated canary traffic test post-config-change that simulates 2x expected RPS for 10m.
sre-rotation: scheduling follow-up postmortem tomorrow 09:30 PT. action items assigned: raj -> revert/validate tier policy CI and add pre-check; ahmed -> write a short test harness for tokenbucket sensitivity; maria -> customer impact summary + support comms; linda -> update runbook with emergency override steps and CLI commands.
maria (oncall): leaving a brief recap for next on-call: scaled pool to 88, tier limit bumped to 120, tokenbucket tuned. queue drained and 429s normalized. handing off to next oncall at 15:00 PT.
ops-bot: incident state -> mitigated. open follow-ups filed: #INC-2026-1745.
raj: one more note — don't forget to roll back the emergency tier cap to a planned value after we validate steady state.
maria (oncall): noted. I'll coordinate with finance for temporary capacity cost approval before we set permanent limits. thanks everyone. :pray:
